<|channel|>analysis<|message|>We need to identify incorrect statement. Let's examine each.

A. Even under extreme noise conditions, SDDPM still can recover most of the high-frequency info. In paper, qualitative results show SDDPM recovers high frequency. They claim robust. Likely correct.

B. The denoising ability of the baseline convolution structure decreases exponentially with the increase of noise. In paper, they discuss that baseline convolution-based models degrade, but they said performance varies arbitrarily within a small interval. They didn't propose exponential decrease. They said performance falls but not stated exponential. So B maybe incorrect. Let's read: “the performance of DnCNN, SCU , SwinIR and SDDPM for different noise levels – The denoising ability of baseline convolution structure decreases exponentially with the increase of noise” Is that mentioned? In discussion: “While DnCNN, SCU, SwinIR have performance decreasing non linearly? They said PSNR and SSIM vary arbitrarily.” Not exponential. So B incorrect.

C. SwinIR's structure contains 3 convolutional layers and a sequence of residual swin transformer blocks (RSTB). Does SwinIR indeed have 3 conv layers? In text: “SwinIR ... involves three phases: shallow feature extraction, deep feature extraction and image reconstruction. The shallow features are extracted by a convolutional layer whereas deep features are extracted by a sequence of residual swin transformer blocks (RSTB) followed by a final convolutional layer.” So actually shallow conv: 1 conv, reconstruction: 1 conv. Combined 2 conv? but maybe another conv? It says shallow feature extraction conv, deep extraction RSTB, image reconstruction conv. That's 2 conv layers. But statement says three conv layers. That seems incorrect. But maybe there is additional conv? Let's verify typical SwinIR architecture: It has one initial conv, then a residual Swin transformer block repeated, then final conv after pixel shuffle. So 2 conv layers. The statement says 3 conv layers – correct or not? The phrase "contains 3 convolutional layers" might be right if there is initial, mid, final? Actually it says three phases: shallow feature extraction, deep feature extraction and image reconstruction. But only shallow and final have CNN. That gives two. But there might be additional conv inside RSTB? But the RSTB contains multi-head self-attention plus MLP, not conv. So likely 2 conv. So statement C is incorrect.

D. One of the time that SDDPM can be used for denoising images obtained from the wild is it is able to map the noisy image to one of the noise levels it has been trained with. The paper states that: "In such a scenario, the model should be able to map the noisy image to one of the noise levels it has been trained with and thereafter generate the denoised image." So D is correct.

Thus we have two potentially incorrect statements, B and C. Which one is more definitely incorrect? The question: "Which of the following statements is incorrect?" Probably only one is incorrect in the paper. Let's check B thoroughly: They mention training set includes noise levels alpha varying [0.005,0.5] and baseline models have erratic performance. In discussion, they say "the PSNR scores for DnCNN, SCU, SwinIR could not show linear trend; they may vary arbitrarily." They didn't mention exponential. So B is incorrect. C: statement mentions 3 conv, but paper says 2 conv. So also incorrect. But maybe the question expects you to recall that SwinIR contains 3 conv: one for shallow, one for deep? But deep is not conv. So it's likely 2 conv. So C incorrect.

But maybe they consider that SwinIR has 3 conv: one shallow, one reconstruction, and one before feeding to transformer? The architecture: Typically SwinIR uses 23 RSTB and then final conv, but also initial conv. That's 2 conv. Might be more if we include upsampling conv. But upsampling conv is part of final conv. So 2. Let's check actual SwinIR paper: It has a shallow feature extraction layer (1 conv), deep feature extraction (multiple RSTB), image reconstruction (1 conv then sub-pixel conv). total 2 conv. There's a final sub-pixel conv after remainder but it's 1 conv too. So maybe 3 conv? Actually reconstruct includes conv + upsample conv? Might be 2 conv inside. So maybe 3? Hard.

Better see the exact statement: "SwinIR's structure contains 3 convolutional layers and a sequence of residual swin transformer blocks (RSTB)." The paper says "The shallow features are extracted by convolutional layer whereas deep features by RSTB then followed by a final convolutional layer." That is 2 conv. So answer likely C. Let's choose C.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>\boxed{C}
